review_method: Independent LLM mathematical verification with exact integer/rational constant checks
checks: The pair-credit argument uses the actual reflected integer bases, so every ambient integer tilt produces endpoint thresholds whose average is the middle threshold. If a good A point is excluded, one homothetic C cap pays the entire A volume; otherwise the actual A cap pays the good subset. The strict support margin and closed endpoint traces are compatible.

All source determinants are taken for actual midpoint simplices (p+C_i)/2 contained in B. Their volumes do not depend on p. The first logarithmic budget remains valid even when there is no good row; the second uses alpha<1/3 and the inverted-simplex contradiction to supply an actual good omitted row. Zero logarithmic weights are accounted for correctly.

Pointwise source credits are measurable affine-threshold sets in each full-dimensional A_i. Integrating the pointwise determinant budget and summing actual pair contributions is justified only by the explicit distinct-base hypothesis, which is present.

The dimension split is exact. For d<=9, alpha<1/64 and the second budget gives correction >53/1116. For d>=10, the differentiated g function is increasing, the exact 693^3>2^28 comparison gives the stated logarithm lower bound, and Gamma_d<=Gamma_7<79/200 gives correction >1/200.

The scalar good-mass curves are continuous because their thresholds are nonconstant affine functions of p; their own-cap terms make them strictly decreasing. The normalized threshold construction therefore produces one actual middle point satisfying every canonical direction lower bound simultaneously.

Pure integer halfspaces contain the middle and at least one endpoint of every reflected pair. Since c_i>=a_i, the resulting raw mass is at least V, so the vertical case is included without discarding boundary mass.

The separate d=1 choice alpha=min(eta,E) satisfies all individual mass ratios. The logarithmic estimate gives the exact 1/2 maximum score, and the sum-of-thresholds argument gives one point satisfying both orientations. These are all nonzero continuous normal directions in dimension one.

The proof explicitly treats the displayed finite source separately from any full induced convex source containing it. It never claims the pairwise midpoint conditions alone characterize all fibers of an arbitrary lifted convex hull.
scope: This is an actual finite reflected-star theorem. It controls all integer tilts for the N positive canonical continuous orientations, and all ambient orientations in d=1. It does not control arbitrary continuous orientations for d>=2, infer the required structural/mass hypotheses for general sources, or compare V automatically to the total mixed mass of an ambient induced set.
